headline: OpenAI adds text watermarking to ChatGPT and Codex in EU
summary: OpenAI is rolling out invisible watermarking for ChatGPT and Codex text, first for EU users to comply with the AI Act, though arstechnica notes such watermarks are not especially reliable and easy to circumvent.

claims.statement: OpenAI is adding an invisible, machine-readable watermark to ChatGPT and Codex text output, starting with EU users.

sources.quote: An invisible, machine-readable watermark in text output is rolling out to ChatGPT and Codex, but only for users in the European Union at first.
OpenAI is preparing to add invisible watermarks to text generated by ChatGPT and Codex in the European Union.

claims.statement: The move is intended to comply with the EU's AI Act transparency rules.

sources.quote: This move is to comply with the EU's new AI transparency rules.
OpenAI will watermark ChatGPT and Codex text in the EU to comply with the AI Act.

claims.statement: Editing text can make the watermark harder to detect, and watermarking is not especially reliable or hard to circumvent.

sources.quote: Editing can make the invisible marks harder to detect, it says.
Like other solutions, it is not especially reliable, and it's easy to circumvent.
